name: EverShelf
description: Self-hosted pantry manager: AI expiry tracking, barcode scanning, smart shopping lists and an Android kiosk for the kitchen wall. Free, open source, no account and no advertising. Product data comes from OpenFoodFacts (millions of items); the AI features need a free Gemini key (see docs). First start: open the Web UI and pair the device with the one-time code printed in the container log: docker logs evershelf 2&1 | grep -i "pairing code" | tail -1 Keep both paths on the array: "App data" holds the database, "Configuration" holds .env.

paths.name: App data
paths.description: SQLite database, caches and logs — this is the pantry. Never put it on a tmpfs: an update would start empty.

paths.name: Configuration
paths.description: Folder holding .env (created from the example on first start, writable by the app).

ports.name: Web UI
ports.description: Port of the web interface (the container listens on 80).

variables.name: Timezone
variables.description: Timezone for expiry dates, logs and cron.

variables.name: Configuration file
variables.description: Where the app reads and writes .env inside the container.
